descriptionChirho: The adjective lach meaning 'moist, fresh, green' — describing something that retains its natural moisture and has not dried out or withered; Arabic طَرِيّ (tariyy) 'fresh/tender' and رَطْب (ratb) 'moist/fresh'; Korean 신선한 (sinseonhan) 'fresh' and 푸른 (pureun) 'green/verdant'; Spanish frescas 'fresh' and verde 'green'; Hindi गीली (gili) 'moist/wet,' ताज़ी (taazi) 'fresh,' and हरा (hara) 'green'; Swahili mbichi 'fresh/raw/unripe.' All 6 occurrences share the core semantic feature of 'retaining moisture, not dried' — whether applied to bowstrings/cords (Judg 16:7,8 fresh/undried cords) or to vegetation (Ezek 17:24 green tree; Gen 30:37 fresh/green rods). The 'fresh' and 'green' translation variants reflect the same underlying quality (moisture-retaining, living) applied to different referents, not genuinely distinct senses.
